Operating Characteristics for Quantitative Decisions Comparing Rates

Source: R/f_design_plan_qtd_rates.R
OperatingCharcteristicsRates.Rd

Stores exact binomial decision-category probabilities for two independent groups. Obtain instances with getOperatingCharacteristicsRates().

Initializes a rates result. Use getOperatingCharacteristicsRates() to validate inputs and calculate probabilities.

Prints the result to the console.

Internal rendering method used by standard console and Markdown output.

Returns the result description used in output headings.

Arguments

design

The originating quantitative decision rule.

numberOfSubjects

Matrix of control and treatment sample sizes.

pi1

Vector of treatment event probabilities.

pi2

Single control event probability.

directionUpper

Whether larger treatment event rates are beneficial.

intervalMethod

Risk-difference interval construction.

probabilities

Computed probability data frame.

showType

Output mode passed to ParameterSet.

digits

Optional display precision.

consoleOutputEnabled

Whether to print or collect the output.

startWithUpperCase

Whether to capitalize the first character.

Details

Inherits the sample-size matrix and probability table from OperatingCharcteristics. The originating quantitative decision rule is stored internally. Each sample-size scenario contains six frequentist or four Bayesian categories and the supplied treatment rates in their original order, including repeats. Console and Markdown printing use the standard ParameterSet mechanism. Use summary() for decision-rule assumptions and probability tables, and plot.OperatingCharcteristics() for the shared QTD plot families.

Fields

groups

Number of independent treatment groups, fixed at 2 (control and treatment). Is a single numeric value representing a whole number.

pi1

Supplied numeric vector of true treatment event probabilities between 0 and 1, inclusive. Its order and repeated entries are retained. Every rate is evaluated for every supplied sample-size scenario against the single control probability pi2.

pi2

The assumed probability in the reference group for two-group designs. Is a single numeric value between 0 and 1.

directionUpper

Whether larger treatment event probabilities are beneficial. TRUE (default) defines the effect as pi1 minus pi2; FALSE defines it as pi2 minus pi1. Reference values use the same beneficial-effect scale. Is a single logical value.

intervalMethod

Frequentist interval construction: qtd1, farringtonManning, miettinenNurminen or newcombe. NA for Bayesian rates, which evaluate posterior criteria instead of confidence intervals. Is a single character value.

alternative

Derived true risk differences in the beneficial direction, one per supplied treatment rate: pi1 minus pi2 when directionUpper is TRUE, otherwise pi2 minus pi1. Entries are between -1 and 1, inclusive, in the same order as pi1, and are not additional user-supplied assumptions. Is a numeric vector.

Inherited fields

probabilities

Calculated data frame of decision-category probabilities. Frequentist results store six categories; Bayesian results store Go, Indeterminate 1, Indeterminate 2 and Stop. Within each sample-size scenario, categories form blocks retaining supplied effect order and repeats. Probabilities are on the scale 0 to 1.

priorDist

Supplied normal-mixture effect prior (RBesT normMix) or a two-element list of control and treatment mean priors, in that order. NULL for frequentist results and rates results. Default Bayesian effect prior is mixnorm(c(1, 0, 100)).

priorDist1

Supplied RBesT betaMix prior for the treatment event probability. NULL for frequentist results and means results. Default Bayesian prior is mixbeta(c(1, 1/3, 1/3)).

priorDist2

Supplied RBesT betaMix prior for the control event probability. NULL for frequentist results and means results. Default Bayesian prior is mixbeta(c(1, 1/3, 1/3)).

controlMean

Single supplied true control mean when separate Bayesian mean priors are used. The true treatment mean is controlMean plus alternative. NULL for an effect prior, frequentist results and rates results.

See also

getOperatingCharacteristicsRates(), getDesignQuantitative()
